top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic OCBC Cycle Singapore's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
When someone attacks on flat to gently rolling urban/highway, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
OCBC Cycle Singapore's flat to gently rolling urban/highway forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 24 miles.
24 miles on flat to gently rolling urban/highway burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
OCBC Cycle Singapore's flat to gently rolling urban/highway rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
2-minute all-out efforts on flat to gently rolling urban/highway. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At OCBC Cycle Singapore, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
At OCBC Cycle Singapore, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of OCBC Cycle Singapore. Train it until it feels boring.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what OCBC Cycle Singapore's flat to gently rolling urban/highway actually does to you.
Base fitness for OCBC Cycle Singapore. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
Varied gradients on flat to gently rolling urban/highway demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.

race_overlay.nutrition: Standard hydration and fueling. One bottle per hour minimum. Gel or bar every 45 minutes at race intensity.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Race Simulation, VO2max, and Road Specific to prepare you for 24 miles of flat to gently rolling urban/highway in The Kallang (formerly Singapore Sports Hub), Singapore.
